Observation: - Hagia Irene (Greek: Ἁγία Εἰρήνη, "Holy Peace", Turkish: "Aya İrini") is a former Eastern Orthodox church converted to a mosque and now a museum in the outer courtyard of Topkapı Palace in Istanbul. It is one of the few churches in Istanbul that was not converted into a mosque, as it was used as an arsenal for centuries.
- Hagia Sophia: Hagia Sophia (from Koinē Greek: Ἁγία Σοφία, romanized: "Hagía Sophía"; lit. 'Holy Wisdom'), officially the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (Turkish: "Ayasofya-i Kebir Cami-i Şerifi"), and formerly the Church of Hagia Sophia, is a Late Antique place of worship in Istanbul, designed by the Greek geometers Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles. Built in 537 as the patriarchal cathedral of the imperial capital of Constantinople, it was the largest Christian church of the eastern Roman Empire (the Byzantine Empire) and the Eastern Orthodox Church, except during the Latin Empire from 1204 to 1261, when it became a Roman Catholic cathedral.
